anchors.statement: The installer must accept --github and --azure flags that select the provider commands rendered into the sc-compose templates.
anchors.quote: could we add --github and --azure flags which inject the proper commands into sc-compose j2 templates?
anchors.summary: Installer --github/--azure select template commands
anchors.scope: adds or changes the installer, provider vars files, sc_render or templates that run PR commands
anchors.deterministic_check: atm-bd skill --azure renders a dispatch template containing 'az repos pr' and no 'gh pr'

pass: The installer gains --github and --azure flags (install.py, test_install_provider_flags) and the chosen provider's command set is merged into the template render context; see the PR diff of install.py.
fail: Templates keep hard-coded gh pr commands and the installer has no provider flag.

anchors.statement: The lite profile's task-close hook business logic must live in a single Python file, skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/atm-bd-task-hook.py.
anchors.quote: The business logic is to be in a single small python file which is organized by transition type and enums w/ exhaustive checks (that will compile error if not handled)
anchors.summary: Lite hook business logic in one file
anchors.scope: adds or changes the lite hook or moves hook logic into another module
anchors.deterministic_check: skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts contains one hook file and no other module imports or defines transition handling

pass: All dev, fix and qa close transitions are implemented in skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/atm-bd-task-hook.py, one section per transition.
fail: The lite close logic is split across hook.py, qa_close.py and dispatch.py helper modules.

anchors.statement: Transitions in the lite hook must be enum members with exhaustive checks, so that an unhandled member is a static error.
anchors.quote: The business logic is to be in a single small python file which is organized by transition type and enums w/ exhaustive checks (that will compile error if not handled)
anchors.summary: Transitions are enums with exhaustive checks
anchors.scope: adds or changes transition handling in the lite hook
anchors.deterministic_check: pyright strict with reportMatchNotExhaustive=error passes on the hook and a test removing one match arm makes it fail

pass: Transition is a StrEnum and every handler uses match with no default arm; pyright strict with reportMatchNotExhaustive=error passes on the hook (pyright output in the PR, test_transition_exhaustive).
fail: Transitions are compared as strings in if/elif chains with a final else that logs unknown.

anchors.statement: Test code written in the phase must implement its repeated patterns through common helper methods instead of repeating them inline.
anchors.quote: test code is fine, but should be written efficiently w/ repeated patterns using common methods.
anchors.summary: Repeated test patterns use common helpers
anchors.scope: adds or changes Python tests in atm-bd-orchestration
anchors.deterministic_check: no setup or assertion block of five or more identical lines appears in two test functions of the touched test files

pass: Tests build hooks through the shared make_close_vars() and run_hook() helpers in tests/lite/conftest.py; no test repeats that setup inline (diff of tests/lite/test_hook.py).
fail: Each test repeats the twelve-line close-vars setup and subprocess stub inline.

anchors.statement: atm-bd cron, atm-bd console and atm-bd queues must be invoked with the same subcommands and arguments for a lite phase as for a full phase.
anchors.quote: We should use the same tool interfaces for atm-bd cron, atm-bd console, atm-bd queues (and others I may have missed).
anchors.summary: Same tool interfaces for every profile
anchors.scope: adds or changes atm-bd console, cron, queues, sprint-report or bv-analyze
anchors.deterministic_check: the --help output of atm-bd console, cron and queues is byte-identical before and after the phase

pass: atm-bd console, cron and queues read the profile from the phase toml and render a lite phase with the same arguments as today; their --help output is byte-identical before and after (tests/test_cli_help_unchanged.py).
fail: A new atm-bd lite-console command is added for lite phases.

anchors.statement: All profiles must use the same schema.
anchors.quote: This would mean that there would need to be atm-bd-core types that are shared between all profiles and I expect we would want the same schema, although atm-bd-lite would allow some mandetory schema items to be 'undefined' i.e. sanity.
anchors.summary: One bead schema for all profiles
anchors.scope: adds or changes bead_schema, close_fields, bead models or formulas
anchors.deterministic_check: no schema file exists under skills/atm-bd-lite and lite beads validate against the core bead_schema models

pass: Lite beads validate against the core bead_schema models; no schema file is added under skills/atm-bd-lite.
fail: skills/atm-bd-lite/schemas/lite-dev-bead.schema.json defines a separate lite schema.

anchors.statement: The shared schema must allow the lite profile to leave its sanity items undefined.
anchors.quote: This would mean that there would need to be atm-bd-core types that are shared between all profiles and I expect we would want the same schema, although atm-bd-lite would allow some mandetory schema items to be 'undefined' i.e. sanity.
anchors.summary: Lite leaves sanity schema items undefined
anchors.scope: adds or changes bead_schema, close_fields or close vars
anchors.deterministic_check: a lite close-vars file without any sanity key validates, and a full close-vars file without them is rejected

pass: sanity_bead and max_sanity_rounds are NotRequired in CloseFields (core/scripts/close_fields.py) and a lite close-vars file without them validates (test_lite_close_vars_without_sanity).
fail: Lite close vars set sanity_bead to the string none to satisfy the required field.

anchors.statement: Scripts and templates of either profile never invoke the gh stack subcommand.
anchors.quote: This is something we should address at ATM BD lite phase buy only checking the base and top of work trees, not using the GH stack sub command
anchors.summary: Never gh stack
anchors.scope: adds or changes stack linking, stack checks, sanity-stack-link, or dispatch templates
anchors.deterministic_check: grep -rn 'gh stack' plugins/atm-bd-orchestration/skills plugins/atm-bd-orchestration/core finds only prose

pass: sanity-stack-link records layers in the stack bead and sets the PR base with the provider command; grep -rn 'gh stack' plugins/atm-bd-orchestration returns prose only, no command (CI grep log attached).
fail: The lite hook calls gh stack link to attach the layer.

anchors.statement: The stack check must verify stacking by comparing only the PR base and the stack top branch, using no other stack record.
anchors.quote: This is something we should address at ATM BD lite phase buy only checking the base and top of work trees, not using the GH stack sub command
anchors.summary: Stack check compares base and top only
anchors.scope: adds or changes the stack gate or stack linking
anchors.deterministic_check: stack_gate.py calls git merge-base and reads the PR base ref and no other stack source

pass: The stack check compares the PR base ref with the stack top branch and reads no other stack record; stack_gate.py makes no gh or API call (test_stack_gate_git_only, PR diff of stack_gate.py).
fail: The stack check queries the GitHub stacks API for the stack's top PR.

anchors.statement: The dev and fix close hook must compare the PR base with the stack top (the branch of the layer below) and block the close when they differ, before it runs bd close and atm task close.
anchors.quote: 1) dev/fix 'atm task close' would check pr base vs. stack top (blocking close if not stacked properly) then do bd close, atm task close.
anchors.summary: Close hook blocks on PR base vs stack top mismatch
anchors.scope: adds or changes a dev or fix close hook or the stack gate
anchors.deterministic_check: a hook test with a mis-based PR exits non-zero and records no bd close or atm task close command

pass: The dev close hook compares the PR base with the stack top first and exits 2 when they differ; bd close and atm task close run only after that check passes (test_hook_blocks_misbased_pr records no bd or atm command).
fail: The hook runs bd close first and then warns that the PR base does not match the stack top.

anchors.statement: All beads of a phase must carry the same profile value (lite or full) as the phase file.
anchors.quote: 2) never mix profiles in the same phase.
anchors.summary: One profile per phase
anchors.scope: adds or changes phase-config, validate-plan, bead-groups or bead_schema
anchors.deterministic_check: validate-plan exits non-zero on a phase file whose beads carry two profiles

pass: validate-plan rejects a lite phase that contains a stage:dev-sanity bead with exit 5 (test_validate_plan_mixed_profiles; run log in the PR).
fail: A phase mixes lite sprints and full sprints by setting the profile per sprint bead.

anchors.statement: Lite-only scripts must live in skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts and lite-only templates in skills/atm-bd-lite/templates; full-only ones live relative to the atm-bd-orchestration skill.
anchors.quote: i would expect the atm-bd-lite only scripts to be in skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/  and templates in atm-bd-lite/templates/ w/ corresponding atm-bd-orchestration scripts/stemplates located relative to the skill.
anchors.summary: Profile-only files under the profile skill
anchors.scope: adds or moves scripts or templates of a profile
anchors.deterministic_check: every file under skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts and templates is imported or rendered only by lite; core/ holds nothing lite-only

pass: atm-bd-task-hook.py, lite_cron.py and the lite dev/fix/qa templates sit under skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts and skills/atm-bd-lite/templates.
fail: The lite hook is placed in core/scripts next to the shared modules.

anchors.statement: Shared scripts and templates must live at one common point, .atm-bd/scripts and .atm-bd/templates at the repository root, removing the duplicates under .claude, .codex and .agents.
anchors.quote: scripts/templates would be at a common point (which perhaps would best be at repo root in .atm-bd/scripts and /templates.  That would remove duplicates across .claude/ .codex/ and .agents/ that exist today
anchors.summary: Shared files installed once to .atm-bd
anchors.scope: adds, moves or installs shared scripts or templates
anchors.deterministic_check: after atm-bd skill install, each shared module exists once under .atm-bd and diff finds no copy under .claude, .codex or .agents

pass: core/scripts and core/templates install to .atm-bd/scripts and .atm-bd/templates; the skill directories no longer carry copies.
fail: Shared modules are copied into .claude/skills and .codex/skills on install as before.

anchors.statement: The atm-bd-lite skill must have its own task-hook Python file, separate from the atm-bd-orchestration skill's atm-task-close.py.
anchors.quote: the atm-bd-lite would have a completely different atm-task-hook python file.
anchors.summary: Lite has its own task hook file
anchors.scope: adds or changes a task-close hook, or selects a hook by profile
anchors.deterministic_check: skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts contains a hook file and the full profile's atm-task-close.py has no lite branch

pass: skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/atm-bd-task-hook.py is a separate file; atm-task-close.py is unchanged.
fail: atm-task-close.py gains an if profile == lite branch that skips sanity.

anchors.statement: The lite profile's orchestration must be runnable by a single agent.
anchors.quote: it will be a much simpler orchestration that could be run by a single agent or small team.
anchors.summary: Lite runs with one agent
anchors.scope: adds or changes the lite skill, lite formulas or lite templates
anchors.deterministic_check: the bo-7 live lite phase log shows one ATM identity performing dispatch, dev, QA and landing

pass: The live lite phase log in bo-7 shows one ATM identity performing dispatch, dev, QA and landing; the lite formula pours only dev and qa beads (atm-bd queues output attached).
fail: The lite formula pours a sanity bead that a second agent must close before QA can start.

anchors.statement: New or rewritten Python code in the phase must return Result<T,Err> values instead of throwing exceptions.
anchors.quote: use pyright, return Result<T,Err> (no throwing)
anchors.summary: Result values, no throwing
anchors.scope: adds or rewrites Python code in atm-bd-orchestration
anchors.deterministic_check: grep raise in the files created by the phase finds only programmer-error guards; every public function returns Ok or Err

pass: profile.py returns Result[Profile]; main maps Err to exit code 2 and JSON output.
fail: load_provider raises ValueError on an unknown provider and callers catch it.

anchors.statement: The fundamental atm-bd types must be defined in one Rust crate.
anchors.quote: I am fine w/ you building a rust crate w/ the fundamental types if it can easily be distributed.
anchors.summary: Fundamental types in one Rust crate
anchors.scope: adds or changes shared enums, error types, provider or stack-gate types, or their distribution
anchors.deterministic_check: crates/atm-bd-types defines Profile, Provider, Transition and Error and no Python module redefines them

pass: The Profile, Provider and Transition enums and the Error type are defined in crates/atm-bd-types and exposed to Python through its wheel.
fail: The shared enums are defined in Python dataclasses under core/scripts and no Rust crate exists.

anchors.statement: A quick Python-only fix of atm-bd must release without a crate publish step.
anchors.quote: I am hopeful we won't be changing the atm-bd crate too often so we don't need a complicated publish process for quick python fixes
anchors.summary: Python fixes release without the crate
anchors.scope: adds or changes release workflows, version files or the crate pin
anchors.deterministic_check: release.yml for a Python-only tag runs no crate publish job

pass: atm-bd 0.21.1 shipped a Python-only fix: release.yml ran no crate publish job and atm-bd-types stays at 0.2.0 (workflow run log and the crates.io version page).
fail: Every Python release bumps and republishes atm-bd-types at the same version number.

anchors.statement: The lite task-hook file must be organized by transition type: one handler section per transition (dev close, fix close, QA close).
anchors.quote: The business logic is to be in a single small python file which is organized by transition type and enums w/ exhaustive checks (that will compile error if not handled)
anchors.summary: Hook organized by transition type
anchors.scope: adds or changes the lite hook
anchors.deterministic_check: the hook file has one handler per Transition member and no handler serves two transitions

pass: atm-bd-task-hook.py has one handler section each for dev close, fix close and qa close, selected by the Transition enum (file outline in the PR; test_one_handler_per_transition).
fail: The hook is organized by bead field, with one function per close-vars key that branches on the transition inside.

anchors.statement: Types shared between all profiles must be defined in atm-bd-core.
anchors.quote: This would mean that there would need to be atm-bd-core types that are shared between all profiles and I expect we would want the same schema, although atm-bd-lite would allow some mandetory schema items to be 'undefined' i.e. sanity.
anchors.summary: Shared types live in atm-bd-core
anchors.scope: adds or changes enums, dataclasses, models or schema types used by a profile or a shared tool
anchors.deterministic_check: no module under skills/atm-bd-lite or skills/atm-bd-orchestration defines a type imported by another skill or by core

pass: Profile, Provider and Transition are defined once in atm-bd-core (crates/atm-bd-types, re-exported by core/scripts) and imported by both profile hooks; grep finds no second definition (PR diff).
fail: skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/types.py defines its own Transition enum copied from the full profile.

anchors.statement: Stack linking and the stack check in both profiles must work on an Azure Git repository, not only on GitHub.
anchors.quote: One item that also needs to be addressed both ATM – BD – lite and ATM – BD – orchestration is for GH stacking to work on non-GitHub repos, a.k.a. azure git repos.
anchors.summary: Stacking works on Azure Git repos
anchors.scope: adds or changes stack linking, the stack gate, or provider commands
anchors.deterministic_check: a stack gate test against an Azure-style remote URL passes and the azure render of the dispatch templates contains az repos pr commands

pass: Stack linking and the stack check both pass against an Azure-style remote: test_stack_gate_azure_remote maps an Azure Git URL to a local bare repository with git insteadOf, and test_stack_link_azure links a layer on it with az repos pr commands (test log in the PR).
fail: The stack check requires the gh CLI and a GitHub remote; Azure repositories are out of scope.

anchors.statement: Python files created or changed in the phase must pass pyright.
anchors.quote: use pyright, return Result<T,Err> (no throwing)
anchors.summary: Touched Python passes pyright
anchors.scope: adds or rewrites Python code in atm-bd-orchestration
anchors.deterministic_check: pyright on the files in the phase diff reports 0 errors

pass: profile.py and providers.py carry # pyright: strict and pyright reports 0 errors on them.
fail: The new provider module is excluded from pyright because of untyped dict access.
